title: Map Scales: Distance and Area
seo_title: Sec 2 Map scales Worksheets: Free Secondary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 maths worksheets on map scales: map distance to actual distance, actual distance to map distance, writing scales as 1 : n, and area scales. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A scale of 1 : n means 1 cm on the map is n cm in real life.
key_sub: There are 100 000 cm in 1 km. For area, square the length scale.
body_html:
How it works

  • A scale of 1 : n means 1 cm on the map is n cm in real life.
  • Map to real: multiply by n, then change units (100 cm = 1 m, 100 000 cm = 1 km).
  • Real to map: change to cm first, then divide by n.
  • Area: if 1 cm represents k km, then 1 cm² represents k² km². Square the length scale.
Example

A map has scale 1 : 50 000. Two places are 6 cm apart. Find the actual distance.

6 × 50 000 = 300 000 cm

300 000 cm = 3 km

Answer: 3 km

Example

1 cm represents 2 km. A lake is 5 cm² on the map. Find its actual area.

1 cm² represents 2² = 4 km²

5 × 4 = 20

Answer: 20 km²

Common mistakes

  • Using 1000 cm in a km. There are 100 000 cm in 1 km.
  • Using the length scale for area. Square it: 1 cm : 3 km gives 1 cm² : 9 km².
  • Writing the scale backwards as n : 1.
  • Multiplying when you need the map distance. Real to map means divide.

faq.q: What does a map scale of 1 : 50 000 mean?
faq.a: 1 cm on the map stands for 50 000 cm in real life, which is 500 m or 0.5 km.

faq.q: How do you change a map distance into kilometres?
faq.a: Multiply the map distance in cm by the scale number, then divide by 100 000 to change cm into km.
Square the length scale. If 1 cm represents 2 km, then 1 cm² represents 4 km².
The one with the smaller scale number, such as 1 : 10 000 compared with 1 : 100 000, because 1 cm covers less ground.
